write.desc: The theorems that say when a limit of functions may be swapped with continuity, integration or differentiation, restated for series of functions, together with the Weierstrass M-test as the standard way to get the uniform convergence they need. These belong together because each one is a precise answer to the question of which hypothesis makes an interchange of limits legitimate.

points.name: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
points.what: Prove with the epsilon/3 argument that if continuous functions f_n converge uniformly to f on a set, then f is continuous, and see exactly where uniformity is used (one N chosen for all points at once).
outside: definition of uniform convergence of a sequence of functions
epsilon-delta definition of continuity at a point

points.name: Continuity theorem as an interchange of two limits
points.what: Read the continuity theorem as lim_{x->c} lim_n f_n(x) = lim_n lim_{x->c} f_n(x), and prove the general version: if f_n -> f uniformly and each f_n has a limit A_n at c, then (A_n) converges and its limit is the limit of f at c.
outside: limit of a function at a point

points.name: Uniform limit of integrable functions is integrable
points.what: Prove that if Riemann integrable f_n converge uniformly to f on [a,b], then f is Riemann integrable, by comparing the upper and lower Darboux sums of f with those of f_n.
outside: Riemann integrability criterion: upper minus lower Darboux sum can be made smaller than epsilon
definition of uniform convergence of a sequence of functions

points.name: Passing a limit through the integral
points.what: Prove that uniform convergence on [a,b] gives lim_n of the integral of f_n equal to the integral of f, using the estimate |integral of (f_n - f)| <= (b-a) sup|f_n - f|, and see why the estimate needs a bounded interval and fails for the moving or growing bump.
outside: properties of the Riemann integral: linearity and the bound |integral of g| <= (b-a) sup|g|

points.name: Differentiating a limit: the term-by-term differentiation theorem
points.what: Prove that if differentiable f_n on [a,b] converge at one point and f_n' converge uniformly to g, then f_n converge uniformly to some f, f is differentiable and f' = g; know why uniform convergence of f_n alone is not enough (sin(nx)/sqrt(n)).

points.name: Series of functions and their uniform convergence
points.what: Treat sum f_n as the sequence of its partial sums, define pointwise and uniform convergence of a series, and use the Cauchy criterion for series (sup over x of |f_{m+1} + ... + f_n| small) and the necessary condition sup|f_n| -> 0.
outside: definition of pointwise and uniform convergence of a sequence of functions
convergence of a series of numbers as the limit of its partial sums

points.name: Interchange theorems for series
points.what: Restate the three interchange theorems for series: a uniformly convergent series of continuous functions has a continuous sum, a uniformly convergent series on [a,b] can be integrated term by term, and a series can be differentiated term by term when the series of derivatives converges uniformly and the series converges at one point.

points.name: The Weierstrass M-test
points.what: Prove that if |f_n(x)| <= M_n for all x in the set and sum M_n converges, then sum f_n converges uniformly and absolutely on that set.
outside: comparison test for series of nonnegative numbers
Cauchy criterion for convergence of a series of numbers

points.name: Using the M-test in practice
points.what: Find good bounds M_n by computing or estimating sup|f_n| (often with calculus), restrict to smaller sets when the bound fails on the whole domain (for example sum x^n on [-r,r] with r < 1), and recognise when the M-test cannot apply although the series still converges uniformly (for example sum (-1)^n/(n+x)).
outside: finding the maximum of a function on an interval with derivatives

points.name: Justifying a swap in an exercise
points.what: Given a limit, integral or derivative to move past a limit or a sum, pick the right interchange theorem, check each of its hypotheses explicitly (usually via the sup-norm or the M-test), and write the justification in a proof; recognise which hypothesis fails in the standard counterexamples.
outside: standard counterexamples to pointwise interchange: x^n on [0,1], the moving bump, sin(nx)/sqrt(n)

points.name: Dini's theorem (optional)
points.what: Prove that if continuous functions on a compact set converge monotonically and pointwise to a continuous limit, then the convergence is uniform, and see by examples that each hypothesis (compactness, monotonicity, continuity of the limit) is needed.
outside: compactness of a closed bounded interval (Heine-Borel or Bolzano-Weierstrass)
definition of pointwise and uniform convergence of a sequence of functions

points.name: A continuous nowhere-differentiable function
points.what: Show with the M-test and the continuity theorem for series that the Weierstrass function (or Abbott's sawtooth sum of h(2^n x)/2^n) is continuous everywhere, and follow a sketch of why it has no derivative at any point.
outside: derivative as the limit of difference quotients

where.title: Stephen Abbott, Understanding Analysis (2nd ed.)
where.detail: Chapter 6: Sections 6.2 (uniform convergence and continuity), 6.3 (uniform convergence and differentiation), 6.4 (series of functions, M-test); Section 7.4 for the integrable limit theorem; Section 5.4 for a continuous nowhere-differentiable function

where.title: Walter Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis (3rd ed.)
where.detail: Chapter 7, Sequences and Series of Functions: uniform convergence and continuity, integration, differentiation, the M-test, Dini's theorem, and the nowhere-differentiable continuous function

where.title: Robert G. Bartle and Donald R. Sherbert, Introduction to Real Analysis
where.detail: Section 8.2 (Interchange of Limits, including Dini's theorem) and Section 9.4 (Series of Functions, Weierstrass M-test)
